span.label: A METHODS GUIDE THAT MAKES `FIND THE COMPETING DEFINITIONS` A REQUIRED STEP, IN A CHECKLIST: `Conceptualization: What is this all about? What are the core concepts you are addressing? And ARE YOU BEING TRUE TO THEIR CORE MEANING? WHAT ARE COMPETING DEFINITIONS? WHICH IS BEST SUITED TO THE TASK AND WHY? Does the SYSTEMATIZED CONCEPT you've selected reflect an adequate understanding of the BACKGROUND CONCEPT? HOW DO DOMAIN EXPERTS APPROACH THE TOPIC?` This is Adcock and Collier's vocabulary turned into a procedure a researcher is told to follow before touching data - and it is the closest thing in the corpus to a specification of what this project does.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For social and cultural concepts there is no ground truth to appeal to, and definitions are contested and change
span.note: what this limits: validation of any social or cultural concept measure: FOR SOCIAL AND CULTURAL CONCEPTS THERE IS NO ABSOLUTE GROUND TRUTH

span.label: An operationalisation is never a faithful rendering of the concept it stands for
span.note: what this limits: every measured construct in the paper and the genre: OPERATIONALIZATIONS ARE NEVER PERFECT TRANSLATIONS, AND ARE OFTEN REFINED OVER THE COURSE OF AN INVESTIGATION
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Many of the concepts at issue cannot be observed at all, which is what makes validation hard rather than merely laborious
span.note: what this limits: validation in the humanities and social sciences specifically: MANY RELEVANT CONCEPTS ARE FUNDAMENTALLY UNOBSERVABLE, SUCH AS LATENT TRAITS OF POLITICAL ACTORS - unlike tasks such as SPAM FILTERING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Human labels are not neutral either - they carry the annotators' priors and perspectives
span.note: what this limits: any human-labelled ground truth: WHEN THE GROUND TRUTH COMES FROM PEOPLE, IT MAY BE INFLUENCED BY IDEOLOGICAL PRIORS, PRIORS, PRIMING, SIMPLE DIFFERENCES OF OPINION OR PERSPECTIVE

span.label: Born-digital data → unobtrusive measurements
span.note: Because born-digital sources do not require direct elicitation, they enable unobtrusive measurement. Enables is absent from the governed types, and the gate correctly refused a causes edge without its governed effect cue.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Domain experts → qualitative insights
span.note: Domain experts identify qualitative insights that can strengthen computational analysis and enrich the answer. Advises/contributes is not a governed relation type.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: black box APIs → data biases
span.note: Closed commercial APIs are likely to introduce biases whose form and severity researchers cannot inspect. Introduces-risk-of is not a governed type, and the wording is probabilistic.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: matching design → control group
span.note: The matching design populates the control group with untreated forums similar to the treated ones. Constructs/selects is absent from the governed types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: control group → counterfactual scenario
span.note: The matched control group is used to estimate what would have happened without the closures. Estimates-counterfactual is absent and should not be forced into operationalised-as without its governed cue.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Discretization → validity
span.note: Overly broad discretized categories can threaten validity. Threatens is absent from the governed types, and deterministic causation would overstate 'can'.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: unit of text → unit of analysis
span.note: The labeled unit of text can differ from the final unit of analysis. Differs-in-level-from is not captured by the governed identity or distinction types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: expert annotators → reliable results
span.note: Highly trained or expert annotators tend to produce more reliable results for complex concepts. Suitable-for/tends-to-improve is absent and explicitly hedged.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: pre-processing steps → reproducibility efforts
span.note: Preprocessing choices have a large impact on reproducibility efforts. Affects is absent from the governed relation types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: post-hoc explanations → models that are already somewhat interpretable
span.note: Post-hoc explanations are an alternative to restricting analysis to models that are already somewhat interpretable, but may be unfaithful. Alternative-to-with-fidelity-risk is absent.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: number of topics → needs of the user
span.note: The appropriate topic count is determined by the needs of the user rather than the collection. Determined-by-analytical-purpose is absent from the governed types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: explanatory power → predictive performance
span.note: For insight-driven studies, improving explanatory power can be more useful than small predictive-performance gains. Preferred-over-for-purpose is absent from the governed types.

span.label: qualitative analyses → Computational text analysis
